passages.text: Now when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and had achieved all that he had desired to do, the LORD appeared to him a second time, as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
Solomon built the house of the LORD.
Solomon also built the royal palace.
Solomon completed everything he wanted to do.
After Solomon finished all his building projects, the LORD appeared to him.
This was the second time the LORD appeared to Solomon.
The LORD had appeared to Solomon before at Gibeon.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ כְּכַלּ֣וֹת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֥וֹת אֶת־ בֵּית־ יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ חֵ֣שֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָפֵ֖ץ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה שֵׁנִ֑ית כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלָ֖יו בְּגִבְעֽוֹן׃

passages.text: And the LORD said to him: “I have heard your prayer and petition before Me. I have consecrated this temple you have built by putting My Name there forever; My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Solomon.
The LORD said, “I have heard your prayer.
I have heard your plea before Me.
I have made this temple holy.
You have built this temple for Me.
I have put My Name in this temple forever.
My eyes will be there always.
My heart will be there always.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי אֶת־ תְּפִלָּתְךָ֣ וְאֶת־ תְּחִנָּתְךָ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְחַנַּ֣נְתָּה לְפָנַי֒ הִקְדַּ֗שְׁתִּי אֶת־ הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנִ֔תָה לָשֽׂוּם־ שְׁמִ֥י שָׁ֖ם עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם וְהָי֨וּ עֵינַ֧י וְלִבִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, with a heart of integrity and uprightness, doing all I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and ordinances, then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised your father David when I said, ‘You will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Solomon.
God gave Solomon a command.
God said, "You must walk before Me."
You must walk as your father David walked.
David walked with integrity.
David walked with uprightness.
You must do everything I command you.
You must keep My statutes.
You must keep My ordinances.
If you do this, I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever.
I promised this to your father David.
I said, 'You will always have a man on the throne of Israel.'
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם־ תֵּלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנַ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר הָלַ֜ךְ דָּוִ֤ד אָבִ֙יךָ֙ בְּתָם־ לֵבָ֣ב וּבְיֹ֔שֶׁר לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֑יךָ חֻקַּ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃ וַהֲקִ֨מֹתִ֜י אֶת־ כִּסֵּ֧א מַֽמְלַכְתְּךָ֛ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעֹלָ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי עַל־ דָּוִ֤ד אָבִ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־ יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: But if indeed you or your sons turn away from following Me and do not keep the commandments and statutes I have set before you, and if you go off to serve and worship other gods, then I will cut off Israel from the land that I have given them, and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name. Then Israel will become an object of scorn and ridicule among all peoples.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Solomon.
God warned Solomon and his descendants.
God said, “If you or your sons turn away from following Me, I will act.
If you do not keep My commandments and statutes, I will respond.
I have set these commandments and statutes before you.
If you go and serve other gods, I will see it.
If you worship other gods, I will know it.
Then I will cut off Israel from the land I have given them.
I will remove Israel from My presence.
I have given this land to Israel.
I have sanctified this temple for My Name.
I will banish this temple from My presence.
Israel will become an object of scorn among all peoples.
Israel will become a byword and a mockery among the nations.
passages.original: אִם־ שׁ֨וֹב תְּשֻׁב֜וּן אַתֶּ֤ם וּבְנֵיכֶם֙ מֵֽאַחֲרַ֔י וְלֹ֤א תִשְׁמְרוּ֙ מִצְוֺתַ֣י חֻקֹּתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃ וְהִכְרַתִּ֣י אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵעַ֨ל פְּנֵ֤י הָאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־ הַבַּ֙יִת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדַּ֣שְׁתִּי לִשְׁמִ֔י אֲשַׁלַּ֖ח מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑י וְהָיָ֧ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לְמָשָׁ֥ל וְלִשְׁנִינָ֖ה בְּכָל־ הָעַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and will hiss and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’
passages.sermon:
This house is the temple in Jerusalem.
The temple will become ruined.
People will see the ruined temple.
Everyone who passes by will be shocked.
They will be appalled by what they see.
They will hiss in scorn.
They will ask a question.
They will say, “Why did the LORD do this to this land?”
They will also say, “Why did the LORD do this to this temple?”
passages.original: וְהַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה עֶלְי֔וֹן כָּל־ עֹבֵ֥ר עָלָ֖יו יִשֹּׁ֣ם וְשָׁרָ֑ק וְאָמְר֗וּ עַל־ מֶ֨ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כָּ֔כָה לָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְלַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And others will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them—because of this, the LORD has brought all this disaster upon them.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The people will answer.
They will say why this happened.
They will say, “They abandoned the LORD their God.
The LORD brought their ancestors out of Egypt.
But they held on to other gods.
They bowed down to these other gods.
They served these other gods.
Because of this, the LORD brought all this disaster on them.”
passages.original: וְאָמְר֗וּ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָזְב֜וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצִ֣יא אֶת־ אֲבֹתָם֮ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַֽיַּחֲזִ֙קוּ֙ בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ לָהֶ֖ם וַיַּעַבְדֻ֑ם עַל־ כֵּ֗ן הֵבִ֤יא יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הָרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃פ

passages.text: Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built these two houses, the house of the LORD and the royal palace, King Solomon gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
Solomon built two houses.
He built the house of the LORD.
He also built the royal palace.
He finished building after twenty years.
Hiram was king of Tyre.
Hiram helped Solomon.
Hiram gave Solomon cedar logs.
Hiram gave Solomon cypress logs.
Hiram gave Solomon gold.
Hiram gave Solomon everything he wanted.
Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns.
These towns were in the land of Galilee.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ בָּנָ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת־ שְׁנֵ֣י הַבָּתִּ֑ים אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־ בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ חִירָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־ צֹ֠ר נִשָּׂ֨א אֶת־ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה בַּעֲצֵי֩ אֲרָזִ֨ים וּבַעֲצֵ֧י בְרוֹשִׁ֛ים וּבַזָּהָ֖ב לְכָל־ חֶפְצ֑וֹ אָ֡ז יִתֵּן֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה לְחִירָם֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים עִ֔יר בְּאֶ֖רֶץ הַגָּלִֽיל׃

passages.text: So Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect the towns that Solomon had given him, but he was not pleased with them.
passages.sermon:
Hiram was the king of Tyre.
Hiram left Tyre.
He went to see the towns.
Solomon had given these towns to Hiram.
Hiram inspected the towns.
The towns did not please Hiram.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֤א חִירָם֙ מִצֹּ֔ר לִרְאוֹת֙ אֶת־ הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַן־ ל֖וֹ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְלֹ֥א יָשְׁר֖וּ בְּעֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” asked Hiram, and he called them the Land of Cabul, as they are called to this day.
passages.sermon:
Hiram was the king of Tyre.
Solomon was the king of Israel.
Solomon gave Hiram some towns.
Hiram spoke to Solomon.
Hiram said, “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?”
Hiram called these towns the Land of Cabul.
People still call them the Land of Cabul today.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֚ה הֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥תָּה לִּ֖י אָחִ֑י וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כָּב֔וּל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

passages.text: And Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold.
passages.sermon: Hiram was the king of Tyre.\r\nHiram sent gold to King Solomon.\r\nHiram sent 120 talents of gold.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח חִירָ֖ם לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים כִּכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב׃

passages.text: This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon imposed to build the house of the LORD, his own palace, the supporting terraces, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of Israel.
He imposed forced labor on the people.
He did this to build the house of the LORD.
He also built his own palace.
He built the supporting terraces.
He built the wall of Jerusalem.
He built the city of Hazor.
He built the city of Megiddo.
He built the city of Gezer.
passages.original: וְזֶ֨ה דְבַר־ הַמַּ֜ס אֲשֶֽׁר־ הֶעֱלָ֣ה׀ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנוֹת֩ אֶת־ בֵּ֨ית יְהוָ֤ה וְאֶת־ בֵּיתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־ הַמִּלּ֔וֹא וְאֵ֖ת חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֶת־ חָצֹ֥ר וְאֶת־ מְגִדּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־ גָּֽזֶר׃

passages.text: Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh attacked the city of Gezer.
Pharaoh captured Gezer.
Pharaoh set Gezer on fire.
Canaanites lived in Gezer.
Pharaoh killed the Canaanites who lived in the city.
Pharaoh had a daughter.
Pharaoh’s daughter was Solomon’s wife.
Pharaoh gave the city of Gezer to his daughter as a dowry.
passages.original: פַּרְעֹ֨ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֜יִם עָלָ֗ה וַיִּלְכֹּ֤ד אֶת־ גֶּ֙זֶר֙ וַיִּשְׂרְפָ֣הּ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְאֶת־ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בָּעִ֖יר הָרָ֑ג וַֽיִּתְּנָהּ֙ שִׁלֻּחִ֔ים לְבִתּ֖וֹ אֵ֥שֶׁת שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, Lower Beth-horon, Baalath, and Tamar in the Wilderness of Judah, as well as all the store cities that Solomon had for his chariots and horses —whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout the land of his dominion.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon rebuilt Gezer.
He rebuilt Lower Beth-horon.
He rebuilt Baalath.
He rebuilt Tamar in the wilderness of Judah.
He built all the store cities that belonged to him.
He built cities for his chariots.
He built cities for his horsemen.
He built whatever he desired in Jerusalem.
He built whatever he desired in Lebanon.
He built whatever he desired throughout all the land of his rule.
passages.original: וַיִּ֤בֶן שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֶת־ גָּ֔זֶר וְאֶת־ בֵּ֥ית חֹרֹ֖ן תַּחְתּֽוֹן׃ וְאֶֽת־ בַּעֲלָ֛ת וְאֶת־ תָּמָר בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ עָרֵ֤י הַֽמִּסְכְּנוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֣וּ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וְאֵת֙ עָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְאֵ֖ת עָרֵ֣י הַפָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת׀ חֵ֣שֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָשַׁק֙ לִבְנ֤וֹת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ וּבַלְּבָנ֔וֹן וּבְכֹ֖ל אֶ֥רֶץ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: As for all the people who remained of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites (the people who were not Israelites)— their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction —Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
There were people in the land who were not Israelites.
These people were Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Their descendants remained in the land after Israel entered it.
The Israelites could not destroy all of them.
Solomon made these remaining people forced laborers.
They served as forced laborers for Solomon.
They continued in this role up to the present day.
passages.original: כָּל־ הָ֠עָם הַנּוֹתָ֨ר מִן־ הָאֱמֹרִ֜י הַחִתִּ֤י הַפְּרִזִּי֙ הַחִוִּ֣י וְהַיְבוּסִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ מִבְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽמָּה׃ בְּנֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נֹתְר֤וּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־ יָכְל֛וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַֽחֲרִימָ֑ם וַיַּעֲלֵ֤ם שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְמַס־ עֹבֵ֔ד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: But Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
He did not make any Israelites slaves.
The Israelites were his soldiers.
They were his servants.
They were his officers.
They were his captains.
They were the commanders of his chariots.
They were the commanders of his cavalry.
passages.original: וּמִבְּנֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹֽא־ נָתַ֥ן שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה עָ֑בֶד כִּי־ הֵ֞ם אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וַעֲבָדָיו֙ וְשָׂרָ֣יו וְשָׁלִשָׁ֔יו וְשָׂרֵ֥י רִכְבּ֖וֹ וּפָרָשָֽׁיו׃ס

passages.text: They were also the chief officers over Solomon’s projects: 550 supervisors over the people who did the work.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon had many building projects.
He appointed chief officers to oversee these projects.
There were 550 supervisors in total.
These supervisors directed the people who did the work.
passages.original: אֵ֣לֶּה׀ שָׂרֵ֣י הַנִּצָּבִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר עַל־ הַמְּלָאכָה֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וַחֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת הָרֹדִ֣ים בָּעָ֔ם הָעֹשִׂ֖ים בַּמְּלָאכָֽה׃

passages.text: As soon as Pharaoh’s daughter had come up from the City of David to the palace that Solomon had built for her, he built the supporting terraces.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh’s daughter lived in Jerusalem.
She first lived in the City of David.
Solomon was the king of Israel.
Solomon built a palace for Pharaoh’s daughter.
Pharaoh’s daughter moved from the City of David to her new palace.
After she moved, Solomon built the supporting terraces.
passages.original: אַ֣ךְ בַּת־ פַּרְעֹ֗ה עָֽלְתָה֙ מֵעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔ד אֶל־ בֵּיתָ֖הּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּֽנָה־ לָ֑הּ אָ֖ז בָּנָ֥ה אֶת־ הַמִּלּֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD. So he completed the temple.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
He built an altar for the LORD.
Three times each year, Solomon offered burnt offerings on this altar.
He also offered peace offerings on the altar.
He burned incense with these offerings before the LORD.
Solomon completed the temple.
passages.original: וְהֶעֱלָ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֡ה שָׁלֹשׁ֩ פְּעָמִ֨ים בַּשָּׁנָ֜ה עֹל֣וֹת וּשְׁלָמִ֗ים עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֣ה לַיהוָ֔ה וְהַקְטֵ֣יר אִתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְשִׁלַּ֖ם אֶת־ הַבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: King Solomon also assembled a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of Israel.
King Solomon assembled a fleet of ships.
He did this at Ezion-geber.
Ezion-geber is near Eloth.
Eloth is in the land of Edom.
Ezion-geber is on the shore of the Red Sea.
passages.original: וָאֳנִ֡י עָשָׂה֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה בְּעֶצְיֽוֹן־ גֶּ֨בֶר אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֶת־ אֵל֛וֹת עַל־ שְׂפַ֥ת יַם־ ס֖וּף בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: And Hiram sent his servants, men who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon’s servants.
passages.sermon:
Hiram was the king of Tyre.
Hiram sent his servants.
These servants were skilled sailors.
They knew the sea well.
Hiram’s servants joined Solomon’s servants.
They served together in the fleet.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח חִירָ֤ם בָּֽאֳנִי֙ אֶת־ עֲבָדָ֔יו אַנְשֵׁ֣י אֳנִיּ֔וֹת יֹדְעֵ֖י הַיָּ֑ם עִ֖ם עַבְדֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: They sailed to Ophir and imported gold from there—420 talents —and delivered it to Solomon.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nHe assembled a fleet of ships.
\r\nThe ships sailed to Ophir.
\r\nThe men brought back gold from Ophir.
\r\nThey collected 420 talents of gold.
\r\nThey delivered the gold to King Solomon.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אוֹפִ֔ירָה וַיִּקְח֤וּ מִשָּׁם֙ זָהָ֔ב אַרְבַּע־ מֵא֥וֹת וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים כִּכָּ֑ר וַיָּבִ֖אוּ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃פ
